_comment: Chrome MV2 gate signatures read at runtime by the patcher from next to the executable (or the current directory) - not embedded, so it can be updated without a rebuild. Each site: sig is hex starting at the cmp, the jg opcode byte sits at index jgOff, and the masked match count must equal expectedMatches. Add a new version's entry with scripts/derive_milestone.py and verify with its --verify mode; see scripts/README.md and mv2-reversing.md.

sites._comment: Gate B: honor off-store ExtensionSettings/ExtensionInstallForcelist on UNMANAGED Chrome. PolicyLoaderWin::LoadChromePolicy guards its FilterSensitivePolicies(&policy) call with ShouldFilterSensitivePolicies() (inlined to `cmp dword[rsi+0x18],1 ; jg skip`). FilterSensitivePolicies [BLOCKED]-prefixes force-install entries whose update_url != the Chrome Web Store, so on an unmanaged browser a self-hosted extension is dropped (chrome://policy: 'ignored - not from a trusted source'). Flipping the jg to jmp always skips the filter, so platform-source ExtensionSettings is honored. Direction-only flip (same target, no call removed). Blast radius: all sensitive platform policies are honored on unmanaged Chrome (setting those registry keys already requires admin). optional so a miss never blocks MV2. The other FilterSensitivePolicies caller is the chrome://policy/test local-test loader (not this platform path).
sites.name: LoadChromePolicy: skip FilterSensitivePolicies (honor off-store ExtensionSettings on unmanaged Chrome)

milestones.name: 151-linux-arm64
milestones._comment: Linux aarch64 `chrome` ELF (EM_AARCH64 0xB7), 151.0.7922.137 (official arm64 .deb). arm64 has no cmp/jg; each gate is cmp w,#2 ; b.gt and the flip rewrites the B.cond condition GT 0xC->AL 0xE (kind bcond, one byte, imm19 preserved) - the same primitive as 151-macos-arm64 / 151-win-arm64. Google publishes no arm64 Linux debug-info, so the gates were located structurally by the arm64 finder and cross-checked against the same-architecture, symbol-verified 151-win-arm64 / 151-macos-arm64 tables. Like 151-linux (x86_64), IsExtensionAffected is a shared out-of-line predicate.

milestones.name: 152-linux-arm64
milestones._comment: Linux aarch64 `chrome` ELF, 152.0.7977.42 beta (official arm64 .deb) - same build version as 152-win-arm64 / 152-macos-arm64, whose four gate bodies this table matches 1:1 (register allocation aside). B.cond GT->AL flip (kind bcond); shared folded bodies carry expectedMatches=2. Structurally derived (no arm64 Linux symbols) and cross-checked against those two symbol-verified tables.

milestones.name: 151-macos-x64
milestones._comment: macOS Intel slice of the universal Google Chrome Framework, 151.0.7922.138. Seven inlined IsExtensionAffected gate sites (same ManifestV2Handler architecture as Windows 151); the three shared gates are byte-identical to 151-linux, and every site was symbol-verified against the official arm64/x86_64 dSYM (UUID-matched to consumer Chrome). Same jg->jmp flip as Windows/Linux.

milestones.name: 151-macos-arm64
milestones._comment: macOS Apple Silicon slice, 151.0.7922.138. arm64 has no cmp/jg; the mv>=3 early-out is `cmp w,#2 ; b.gt` and the flip rewrites the branch condition GT(0xC)->AL(0xE), keeping imm19 (kind 'bcond'; see mv2-reversing.md). All seven gates were symbol-named from the official arm64 dSYM (UUID 4c4c4467...). The arm64 flip is verified in CI on real Apple Silicon (patch->re-sign->launch->MV2 load) and patched by default like the x86_64 slice.

milestones.name: 151-win-arm64
milestones._comment: Windows-on-ARM native arm64 chrome.dll (PE32+, machine 0xAA64), 151.0.7922.138. Same seven-gate ManifestV2Handler/StandardManagementPolicyProvider architecture as Windows 151 x64; arm64 has no cmp/jg, so each gate is cmp w,#2 ; b.gt and the flip rewrites the B.cond condition GT 0xC->AL 0xE (kind bcond, one byte, imm19 preserved) - the same primitive as 151-macos-arm64. Symbol-verified against the official Windows arm64 chrome.dll PDB.

milestones.name: 152-macos-x64
milestones._comment: macOS Intel slice of the universal Google Chrome Framework, 152.0.7977.42 (consumer beta). Chrome 152 layout; symbol-verified against the official x86_64 dSYM. Same x86 jg flip as Windows/Linux.

milestones.name: 152-macos-arm64
milestones._comment: macOS Apple Silicon slice, 152.0.7977.42 (consumer beta). Chrome 152 layout, B.cond GT->AL flip (kind bcond), symbol-verified against the official arm64 dSYM; a shared folded body covers ShouldBlockExtensionInstallation + UserMayInstall. Patched by default like the x86_64 slice.

milestones.name: 152-win-arm64
milestones._comment: Windows-on-ARM native arm64 chrome.dll (PE32+, machine 0xAA64), 152.0.7977.42 beta. Chrome 152's rearchitected ManifestV2Handler set (same gates as Windows 152 x64); arm64 flips the B.cond GT->AL (kind bcond). Symbol-verified against the arm64 chrome.dll PDB; a shared folded body covers ShouldBlockExtensionEnable + IsExtensionAffected.

milestones.name: 151-chromium-linux-xtradeb
milestones._comment: Distro build (Ubuntu ppa:xtradeb/apps, 151.0.7922.108) - clang inlines the predicate, so this is a 4-site table (not the single free predicate of Google's build). Derived symbol-verified from the PPA's chromium-dbgsym; re-derive after an xtradeb rebuild.

sites._comment: Gate A: grant webRequestBlocking to MV3 extensions. The permission feature's rule-1 SimpleFeatureData (extension_types=[extension,legacy_packaged_app], max_manifest_version=2, no location) is a C++20 designated-initializer POD struct in .rdata; flipping max_manifest_version 2->3 grants the permission to MV3 and nothing else. Located name-anchored (find the 'webRequestBlocking\0' literal, find pointers to it, decode the struct, verify rule-1 criteria). 155-only representation (154 and earlier use the old feature layout); optional so a miss never blocks MV2 patching.
sites.name: webRequestBlocking permission feature rule 1 (max_manifest_version 2->3; grants MV3)
